package.title: Cross-cutting Deep Dive — Safety / Security / Trust Boundary
package.editorial_angle: Safety/Securityを独立ECUへ逃がす前提が崩れると、isolation、resource partitioning、service authentication、deterministic runtimeが各層横断のarchitecture contractになる。
boundaries: The evaluation shows high performance jitter, attributed partly to parallel execution on a single system; Open vSwitch/Mininet emulation also omits physical network transmission times.
Supply-chain attacks, secure builds, OTA distribution and some mixed-security downgrade cases are outside the detailed security analysis.
The main automotive evaluation does not include remote DNSSEC resolution in the service-setup path; the authors expect such resolution to occur during update procedures.
The paper explicitly focuses on initiator-side mechanisms and defers resource-side developments.
The open-source QEMU/CPU/Bao proof-of-concept is presented as a roadmap rather than completed validation in this paper.

For simplicity, the model assumes coexistence/freedom-from-interference criteria are satisfied when mixed-criticality tasks share hardware; the optimization does not itself establish the complete safety argument for that coexistence.
Scalability experiments use a fixed four-ECU architecture with randomly generated task graphs and randomized WCET/WCRT/cost values, limiting direct transfer to a production E/E program.
Reported objective values and solver timings are case-study/problem-instance results rather than universal design-space optimization performance.
The page is authored by DENSO and hosted by SOAFEE; deterministic guarantees and portability/safety benefits are vendor/project claims rather than independent certification evidence.
The pinned article does not provide a sufficiently detailed independent latency/jitter or safety-certification evaluation for quantitative comparison.

artifact.canonical_name: Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services

sources.title: Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The proposal separates supplier-side software/certificate generation from OEM-controlled deployment trust by publishing supplier certificates through OEM-signed DNSSEC TLSA records.

DNSSEC, DANE and DANCE are integrated into automotive publish-subscribe service discovery/authentication/authorization, with an example SOME/IP integration and support for cached/offline verification.
The authors evaluate the design using a STRIDE threat analysis and a realistic in-vehicle setup; the evaluation indicates service setup remains below their cited 200-ms requirement despite jitter.
claims.context: Author security/performance evaluation, not independent certification.

metrics.context: Scale estimate reported from the realistic IVN evaluation.

metrics.name: average TLSA certificates resolved per node for remote peers
service setup requirement referenced by evaluation
metrics.context: Authors report individual-service setup well below this cited requirement.

limitations.text: The evaluation shows high performance jitter, attributed partly to parallel execution on a single system; Open vSwitch/Mininet emulation also omits physical network transmission times.
Supply-chain attacks, secure builds, OTA distribution and some mixed-security downgrade cases are outside the detailed security analysis.
The main automotive evaluation does not include remote DNSSEC resolution in the service-setup path; the authors expect such resolution to occur during update procedures.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary text verifies the DNSSEC/DANE/DANCE trust model, SOME/IP integration, STRIDE analysis, realistic-IVN evaluation, scale figures and explicit jitter/simulation/security-scope limitations.

editorial.why_now_note: As SOA and post-sale software increase multi-supplier dynamism, credential ownership and service authorization become first-class architecture boundaries rather than fixed provisioning details.
editorial.rationale: Strong service/security architecture evidence: it explicitly separates supplier credentials from OEM deployment trust and evaluates a protocol-independent credential lifecycle integrated with SOME/IP.

artifact.canonical_name: RISC-V Needs Secure 'Wheels': the MCU Initiator-Side Perspective
artifact.organization: OSYX Technologies / Universidade do Minho / Infineon AG

sources.title: RISC-V Needs Secure 'Wheels': the MCU Initiator-Side Perspective
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors tie centralized/domain/zone E/E evolution to increasing integration density, where formerly separate ECUs become virtualized logical partitions on fewer physical MCUs and require freedom-from-interference.
The paper argues that then-current RISC-V WorldGuard/SPMP proposals are insufficient for foreseen automotive virtualized-MCU isolation and proposes hypervisor-aware initiator-side extensions.
claims.context: Author technical critique/proposal, not a ratified ISA fact.

claims.text: The proposed Slwgd/related register extensions expand the WorldGuard identifier model toward 64/128 IDs and add virtualized privilege-level delegation support.

metrics.name: maximum World IDs targeted by the proposal
metrics.context: Proposed extension capacity; not a ratified WorldGuard requirement.

metrics.name: estimated WIDs for the paper's high MCU configuration
metrics.context: Author-estimated upper-threshold example based on harts, privilege levels and non-CPU initiators.

limitations.text: The paper explicitly focuses on initiator-side mechanisms and defers resource-side developments.
The open-source QEMU/CPU/Bao proof-of-concept is presented as a roadmap rather than completed validation in this paper.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for RISC-V Needs Secure 'Wheels': the MCU Initiator-Side Perspective; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary text verifies the automotive virtualization/isolation motivation, WorldGuard/SPMP gaps, proposed hypervisor/ID extensions, 128-ID target and explicit PoC/resource-side future-work boundary.

editorial.why_now_note: As ECU consolidation increases mixed-criticality co-location, hardware isolation capability becomes an E/E architectural constraint rather than a local MCU implementation detail.
editorial.rationale: Strong compute-isolation evidence for consolidating formerly separate ECUs into virtualized MCU partitions, while clearly remaining a proposal/roadmap rather than completed proof-of-concept.

artifact.canonical_name: ASIL-Decomposition Based Resource Allocation Optimization for Automotive E/E Architectures

sources.title: ASIL-Decomposition Based Resource Allocation Optimization for Automotive E/E Architectures
sources.role: Author paper/preprint used to verify the reported architecture, method/evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors formulate automotive software-to-hardware mapping, scheduling and ASIL decomposition as a single mixed-integer linear optimization problem targeting development cost and critical-chain execution time while applying safety/reliability constraints.

The exemplary case study exposes a cost/latency trade-off: prioritizing development cost yields lower cost with longer maximum application execution time, while prioritizing latency increases cost and reduces that execution time.
The authors compare Gurobi and CPLEX and report that solving time grows as task count increases; ASIL decomposition cases can materially increase optimization time.
claims.context: Generated/evaluated problem instances, not production design-cycle measurements.

Scalability experiments use a fixed four-ECU architecture with randomly generated task graphs and randomized WCET/WCRT/cost values, limiting direct transfer to a production E/E program.
Reported objective values and solver timings are case-study/problem-instance results rather than universal design-space optimization performance.

editorial.why_now_note: Resource allocation under ASIL and timing constraints is a direct mechanism by which centralized/mixed-criticality E/E architecture choices become computable rather than intuitive.
editorial.rationale: Strong design-method evidence if solver/cost/latency values remain tied to the exemplary case study and FFI assumption.

sources.title: SOAFEE Blueprint: DENSO develops deterministic middleware for SDV
sources.role: SOAFEE-hosted DENSO-authored blueprint used for deterministic middleware architecture, mixed-criticality goals and demonstration framing.

claims.text: DENSO describes using the open-source Lingua Franca time-coordination language to define application behavior and support time-centric scheduling/runtime monitoring.
claims.context: DENSO-authored architecture claim hosted as a SOAFEE blueprint.

claims.text: The blueprint proposes running safety and non-safety workloads in parallel while combining cloud-native technologies with functional-safety and real-time requirements, including application-level safety envelopes and violation detection.
The article states that the first blueprint demonstrates the approach using an Autoware Foundation automated-driving stack.

limitations.text: The page is authored by DENSO and hosted by SOAFEE; deterministic guarantees and portability/safety benefits are vendor/project claims rather than independent certification evidence.
The pinned article does not provide a sufficiently detailed independent latency/jitter or safety-certification evaluation for quantitative comparison.

targets.target: Verify the official scope/status and architecture-significant statements on soafee-denso-deterministic-middleware; distinguish directly checkable facts from organization/project claims.
targets.finding: The blueprint directly verifies the proposed time-centric/mixed-criticality middleware architecture and demonstration framing; its guarantees remain VENDOR_CLAIM.

editorial.why_now_note: The blueprint is a useful industry implementation pattern connecting cloud-native SDV development to deterministic mixed-critical execution.
editorial.rationale: Strong architecture signal if presented explicitly as a DENSO/SOAFEE blueprint rather than neutral proof of deterministic performance.
